text: Contact centers hire at massive scale. But the skill that matters most, how someone actually sounds on a live call with an upset customer, is still screened by hand, one phone interview at a time.

Those phone screens eat hours of recruiter time, and the notes they produce are subjective. Good English. Seems confident. Nobody can check them. And a grammar quiz can't tell you whether someone can calm down a customer whose rent is due tomorrow.

Acuity Voice puts the candidate on a realistic call, and it's built entirely on Assembly A I, in three stages. First, the live call. A Voice Agent plays the customer, with its own persona, voice, and key terms. Second, measure. The candidate's audio is transcribed with Universal three point five Pro, keeping every um and uh, with word timings and confidence, so pace, filler rate, and pauses are computed in code. Third, judge. A second Voice Agent session reads the transcript and returns a structured scorecard through a tool call.
Here's a live demo. To show it hands free, we put two Assembly A I Voice Agents on the same call. An upset customer, and Sam, an A I trainee rep, who gets scored exactly like a human candidate would.

Seconds after the call ends, the readiness report is ready. Readiness is computed in code from five rubric scores, never guessed by the model. The speech metrics come straight from Universal three point five Pro timestamps. And every finding quotes the rep's exact words. If a quote can't be found word for word in the transcript, it's thrown out. Click a timestamp, and you jump straight to that moment in the call.

A few decisions make this reliable. The customer agent has no tools, because tool turns made it go silent mid call. Turn detection stays adaptive, with max accuracy transcription, so nervous candidates aren't cut off. And voice, transcription, and scoring all run on a single Assembly A I key.

For B P O and contact center teams, this turns a subjective phone screen into a consistent, evidence backed report that a reviewer can check in a minute. It's a readiness signal, not an automated hiring decision, so people stay in the loop.
Acuity Voice. Hear the call before you make the hire. Built on Assembly A I.
